New since our last check. An open-source AI chatbot, made for fun, with a real opt-in step: nothing from you reaches the AI until you say yes. Approved for Stoat Discovery while it was offline.
No privacy policy. Its opt-in message doesn't say which AI company gets your messages, people who used it before opt-in were counted as having agreed, and saved memories have no expiry.
Opt-in before anything is sent

Until you say "magbot opt in", your messages are never sent to the AI, never used as context and never answered. Messages from people who haven't opted in are left out of the context it sends for others too.
docs/CONSENT.md
Opting out deletes your memories
Saying "magbot opt out" removes you from the list and deletes everything it has remembered about you. /forget-me deletes your memories without opting out.
No privacy policy

There's a detailed consent document in the code, but no privacy policy telling members what is stored, where, for how long or how to ask for deletion. Stoat has said privacy policies will become a requirement.
The AI company isn't named

The opt-in message says your message and the few around it go to "an AI model". The default settings send them to OpenAI, an outside company. Stoat told us that sending content to an outside AI service needs each person's explicit consent, so the message should say who receives it.
magbot/consent.py#L38-L46
Earlier users counted as agreeing
Everyone who had used magbot before the opt-in system was added to the opt-in list automatically. Using a bot before it asked isn't the same as saying yes.
Memories with no expiry
Facts it remembers about each person are kept in a database until that person deletes them or opts out. Nothing removes them after a set time.

My friend recently got their bot approved for discovery and then informed me after that his bot hasn't been online at all for the review process. This raises serious concerns about how Stoat is keeping the platform safe and how bots are actually verified for discovery listings.
I understand that you cannot comment on individual cases. However I'd like to know a few things:
How was this allowed to happen?
What is the process for reviewing bots for discovery?
What does Stoat do to make sure the bot isn't malicious?
A published review process for Discovery that checks a bot while it's online, including what it does with members' data, before it's listed.

04 / How Discovery bots are checked
A bot was approved for Discovery while it was offline.

Stoat Discovery lists bots for everyone on Stoat to find and add. Being listed tells people Stoat has looked at a bot, so they trust it more. On 12 November 2026, magbot's developer was told its Discovery listing had been approved. The bot had been down for about a month, so it can't have been running while it was reviewed.

A Stoat DM. mag shares a Platform Moderation notice that the Discover listing request for magbot#6581 has been approved, and says the bot has been down for the past month and was only just fixed. Kurome replies that it's very concerning, asking how Discovery can be approved for an offline bot. mag answers: no idea.
The approval notice, shared by magbot's developer on Stoat · 12 November 2026

This isn't about magbot doing anything wrong. It's about what a Discovery approval means. If a bot can be approved without running, nobody can have checked what it does with members' messages, whether it asks for consent or whether it's safe. Every bot should be checked properly when it applies for Discovery, whoever made it.
Our email to Stoat
We emailed Stoat on 12 November 2026 to ask how bots are reviewed for Discovery. This is the email in full, apart from the sign-off:
Hi there,

Discovery is a powerful tool for bot developers to get outreach for their projects. But it can be easily abused if the bot isn't checked properly and the trust of that application goes up significantly because the end-user believes stoat will do the necessary safety checks.
